title: Avoiding the Reverse Fall Trap in Drainage Installations
description: One of the most frequent errors in drainage installation is failing to maintain consistent downward slope, leading to the dangerous practice of reverse fall or bellied pipes. When a drain pipe slopes upward or sags due to improper support, wastewater pools inside the line instead of flowing freely toward the main sewer. Over time, these stagnant pools accumulate grease, sediment, and organic waste, creating chronic blockages and foul odors. Professional installers must always verify proper gradient using precise leveling tools and ensure continuous hanger support according to manufacturer specifications and local code requirements.
